intended_object: A derivation, in any proof system extending minimal logic, of the De Morgan law (¬φ ∧ ¬ψ) → ¬(φ ∨ ψ). The docstring is uninformative, so this is inferred from the name and the type.
explanation: The definition builds a proof term of type `𝓢 ⊢ (∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ) ==> ∼(φ ⋎ ψ)`, which is exactly the De Morgan implication. It holds for any `𝓢` satisfying `Entailment.Minimal`, which is the right setting: this direction of De Morgan is valid in minimal logic, with no need for excluded middle or explosion. The proof turns the conjunction into nested implications and assumes ¬φ, ¬ψ and φ ∨ ψ. It then turns each negation into an implication to ⊥ and does case analysis on the disjunction (`or₃'''`) to derive ⊥, so every step is minimal-logic valid. The statement is correct and stated at its natural generality: any formula type with connectives and any minimal proof system. Mathlib has no abstract Hilbert-style entailment framework, so there is no counterpart to cite.
